checks.title: Account

reviewedElements.difference: Production places each setting in a separate filled card. The prototype uses a compact two-column table for Email, Display Name, Password and Training Data Opt-Out.
Production uses “Account Settings” and places Display Name before Email. The prototype uses “Account” and starts with Email.
Production adds an Organization Role card between Email and Change Password; this section is absent from the prototype.
Production uses full-width fields with labels above them and a “Change Password” button. The prototype uses narrower fields with placeholder labels and a “Change” button.
Production uses a filled card with a solid red heading strip. The prototype uses an outlined red “Danger Zone” block.
The prototype has copyright and legal links below the settings; these are absent from the production capture.

comparisonNotes: Production shows a Developer role and disables training opt-out with an admin-permission message. The prototype explains availability after purchasing credits. These are different access states.

checks.title: Internal: Users

reviewedElements.difference: Production keeps the shared “Users & Organizations” heading and introduction above the tabs. The prototype places the tabs first and gives each section its own heading and introductory text.
Production places a full-width bordered search field above the card. The prototype integrates an icon-led search field into the card header.
The prototype includes a Show test accounts switch beside search; it is absent from the production capture.
Production separates Name and Email. The prototype combines them in the User column and adds a UUID column with a visual identifier and shortened UUID.
The prototype shows a leading chevron on each row; production has no visible expand indicator.

comparisonNotes: Production contains live records and pagination; the prototype contains a small fixture dataset. Names, record counts and values are not design defects. Row details were not opened in this comparison.

reviewedElements.difference: Production rows are taller and use larger colored role badges. The prototype uses compact neutral badges.
Production adds a horizontal divider between the organization list and creation form; the prototype separates them with whitespace.
Production uses a smaller headline, flat model icons with a model description, and a Models Overview link. The prototype uses larger headline text, 3D model icons and a Pricing link.

comparisonNotes: Organization names are replaced with Demo 1 and Demo 2 in both screenshots. Roles belong to different datasets and are not design defects. Selection and creation were not performed.

checks.title: Header: Account menu

reviewedElements.difference: Production adds separate Account Settings and Switch organization rows. The prototype links directly from the email and organization rows.
Production uses a Theme section with System / Light / Dark icon buttons. The prototype uses one Appearance row with a compact toggle.
Production uses a tinted menu surface, larger internal spacing and separators between sections. The prototype has a compact white menu without these section dividers.

comparisonNotes: Production is the user-supplied menu crop; the host URL identifies the shared header, not a separate page. Prototype is an element capture at DPR 2. Capture contexts differ; no pixel score or measured size comparison is assigned.

prototypeNotes.difference: Add System / Light / Dark selection as in production instead of the current two-state Appearance toggle.
Add an explicit organization switching action, matching the production Switch organization entry.
Create the DS pagination component: Previous / Next controls, page numbers, current-page styling and disabled states. Use the production example as a functional reference.

reviewedElements.difference: Production uses different icons; the prototype uses the 3D model icons.

comparisonNotes: The header navigation and footer differ, but the captures show different sign-in states.
